tellings.difference: Here Price's intended target was a cabin in the woods and he described a clandestine site nearby instead; Sheehan's telling says Price was given exact coordinates of a CIA facility.

plain: In the 1970s, a man named Pat Price is said to have used remote viewing, the claimed ability to see a distant place with the mind alone, to describe a secret government site, and even to read a file inside a top-security CIA facility. Dan Sheehan, a guest who says he saw a file on it himself, tells Michels that Price "had gotten so good at remote viewing" that he was given the exact longitude and latitude of the facility and read what was there. Sheehan names the researcher Russell Targ and the remote viewer Ingo Swann, and credits reports Swann made to the Guardian's Office, an arm of the Church of Scientology. Joe McMoneagle, a guest who repeats what Targ and the researcher Hal Puthoff told him, tells it differently. In his version Price was supposed to describe an old cabin in the woods and instead "described a clandestine site" nearby. If either version is true, it would mean the mind can get past the tightest government security.
